Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L05_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

A speaker says, "We should explain the claim before the examples so the audience understands our point." Which response best paraphrases the speaker?

answer.text: A. You think examples do not matter at all.

feedback.text: This changes the meaning. The speaker did not reject examples; the speaker suggested a better order.

answer.text: B. You are saying the claim should come first so the examples make more sense to the audience.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the speaker's meaning and restates it in new words.

answer.text: C. You want to skip the claim and use only examples.

feedback.text: This reverses the message. The speaker wants the claim explained first.

answer.text: D. You are saying the audience is not important.

feedback.text: This misses the main idea. The speaker specifically mentioned audience understanding.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L05_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

What is the main goal of paraphrasing during discussion?

answer.text: A. To restate the speaker's idea in your own words without changing the meaning

feedback.text: Correct. Paraphrasing checks understanding before the discussion moves forward.

answer.text: B. To add your opinion before understanding

feedback.text: This skips the listening step. A paraphrase should show understanding first.

answer.text: C. To make the speaker's idea sound completely different

feedback.text: This changes meaning. A paraphrase should preserve the meaning.

answer.text: D. To copy the speaker's exact words

feedback.text: Paraphrasing uses your own words. Copying exactly is repeating, not paraphrasing.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L05_GuidedPractice_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which response uses the best tone for respectful disagreement?

answer.text: A. Stop talking about that idea.

feedback.text: This shuts down discussion instead of responding respectfully.

answer.text: B. That idea is wrong, and mine is better.

feedback.text: This tone is dismissive. It attacks the idea without explaining a useful reason.

answer.text: C. I disagree because I do not like it.

feedback.text: This gives an opinion but not a communication reason.

answer.text: D. I understand your point, but I see it differently because the audience may need a more serious opening.

feedback.text: Correct. This response acknowledges the speaker, disagrees respectfully, and gives a reason.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L05_GuidedPractice_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

A classmate says, "The tone needs to be different." Which response best clarifies the message?

answer.text: A. That does not help at all.

feedback.text: This expresses frustration but does not ask for clarification.

answer.text: B. When you say different, do you mean more serious or more encouraging?

feedback.text: Correct. This asks a specific clarifying question and gives the speaker a clear way to explain.

answer.text: C. I will ignore that comment.

feedback.text: This avoids the chance to understand the speaker.

answer.text: D. You should know what different means.

feedback.text: This blames the speaker and does not clarify the idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L05_GuidedPractice_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which discussion response best builds on another person's idea?

answer.text: A. I was not listening to that idea.

feedback.text: This does not build on the idea because it shows no understanding.

answer.text: B. Your idea is not part of my section.

feedback.text: This dismisses the group connection instead of building the discussion.

answer.text: C. Your point about audience attention connects to our opening; we could add a short question there.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects to the speaker's idea and adds a useful next step.

answer.text: D. I do not want to discuss that point.

feedback.text: This stops discussion rather than developing the idea.
